title: CLI inventory over loadAllExtensions (scoped down: state/shadowed only, no shadow-source)
wave: M4 Wave D — Khả năng nhìn thấy triage (shippable: false, waits on M4's shared changelog gate, plan §6.2/§6.3)
one_line: Add a read-only `omp extensions-triage` command that prints, for every extension the loader found, whether it is active / disabled / shadowed and which disable policy blocked it, by projecting the exact rows `loadAllExtensions` already returns instead of re-deriving anything.
user_visible_effect: A new top-level CLI command. The user runs `omp extensions-triage` (or `--json`) and sees one row per extension with a state column (`active` / `disabled` / `shadowed`) and a reason column, so they can answer "is my plugin actually loading, and if not, which policy stopped it". The command is a pure projection: it changes no loader state, toggles nothing, and writes no settings. It does NOT name what shadowed a row — that value is `undefined` everywhere in the current tree (see plan_corrections), and inventing it in the CLI is explicitly out of scope.
effort: S for option (a) (~1 day: 2 new files + 2 modified + 1 test). M for option (b) (~2-3 days: option (a) plus a shared-core change in capability/index.ts and a 6-call-site change in state-manager.ts). The plan's "S is optimistic" verdict is correct for (b) only; (a) is genuinely S.
risk: Shipping a CLI that re-derives shadowing independently of `loadAllExtensions`, so the inventory and the runtime dashboard disagree — the plan calls this out and is right: an inventory that lies is worse than no inventory. The concrete way this happens in (a) is passing `undefined` for the `disabledIds` argument: the loader still reads `cfgDisabledExtensions` internally, but the `disabledExtensions` Set that `resolveState` consults stays empty, so the CLI reports item-level-disabled rows as `active` while the TUI dashboard reports them `disabled`. The mirror of acp-agent.ts:1191-1193 is mandatory. For option (b) the top risk is different and mechanical: at both `item._shadowed = true` sites the winning item is not recoverable as the code stands (see plan_corrections #5), so a naive `_shadowedBy = existing._source` edit compiles, type-checks, and silently still yields `undefined`.
depends_on: M2 WI-2 (deterministic extension load order + explicit collision resolution) — MUST be merged before this ships. UNMET as of 2026-09-27: packages/coding-agent/test/extension-load-order-determinism.test.ts does not exist and `git grep -n 'extension-load-order' packages/coding-agent/` returns 0 hits, so WI-2's deliverable is not in the tree. If this CLI ships first, it reports an ordering the user never sees in the dashboard.
Nothing else. Option (a) touches no shared core.
open_questions: (a) or (b)? The plan explicitly refuses to choose and requires the choice to be recorded. DECISION GATE — step 1 below. Recommendation: ship (a) now (it needs no core change and answers the triage question), and file (b) as its own work item rather than bundling a shared capability-core change into a CLI PR.
Command name. Spec uses `extensions-triage`. The registry already has `plugin`, `skill`, `config`; `extensions-triage` is unambiguous against all of them. Confirm before writing the help string.
Default output: table or one-line-per-row? The spec assumes one sanitized line per row, matching the `omp plugin list` shape at packages/coding-agent/src/cli/plugin-cli.ts:644. Confirm.

Does Wave D ship in the same changelog decision as M4 Waves B and C, or does it need its own? Plan §6.2 says all three M4 waves merge as ONE changelog decision and none ships before that decision exists. Confirm the owner has actually granted it — `shippable: false` means this cannot be released on its own.

For option (b): should `_shadowedBy` carry a display string (e.g. `skill:foo` via `makeExtensionId`) or a raw path? Recommend the extension id, because that is what the user can act on and what the TUI inspector already renders at packages/tui/src/overlays/extensions/inspector-model.ts:466-482.

steps.instruction: RECORD THE SCOPE DECISION before writing code. Choose (a) narrow — the CLI reports `state` / `disabledReason` / `shadowed`, never a shadow source — or (b) full — additionally make `shadowedBy` real. Write the choice and one sentence of rationale into the PR description. (a) is the recommendation: it needs no shared-core change, it answers the actual triage question ('is my plugin loaded, and which policy stopped it'), and it keeps a `capability/index.ts` change out of a CLI PR. (b) is a real change to shared discovery state and deserves its own review.

Confirm M2 WI-2 has merged. The gate is `packages/coding-agent/test/extension-load-order-determinism.test.ts` existing. If it does not exist, STOP — this item is blocked. On 2026-09-27 it did not exist, so M4-9 is not startable yet and must queue behind WI-2.

Read the two existing consumers before designing the row shape: `isShadowedExtension` and the `Extension` interface in the tui package, and the `enablementLabel` / `#getStatusBadge` renderers. They decide what a shadowed row is allowed to look like, and they already render a 'Shadowed by X' string that today never receives a value — decide deliberately whether the CLI should mirror that wording or stay independent of it.

OPTION (a): create `packages/coding-agent/src/cli/extensions-triage-cli.ts`. Export a pure `toTriageRow(ext: Extension): ExtensionTriageRow` and a `runExtensionsTriage(args)` that does `Settings.init()` then `cfgDisabledExtensions.get(sm)` then `loadAllExtensions(cwd, disabledIds)`. The disabledIds argument is the whole ballgame: passing `undefined` makes the loader read cfg internally but leaves `resolveState`'s `disabledExtensions` Set empty, so item-level disables report as `active` here and `disabled` in the dashboard. Mirror acp-agent.ts:1191-1193 exactly.

OPTION (a): render. `--json` emits `{ "extensions": [...] }` (precedent: `omp config --json`, `omp skill --json`). Human output is one line per row: id, state, parenthesised disabledReason, provider, shortened path. Run paths through `shortenPath` and tabs through `replaceTabs` from the central helpers — no ad-hoc truncation constants. Use `console.log`: this is a standalone CLI that exits without entering the TUI, which AGENTS.md explicitly permits. If the output ever gets rendered inside the TUI, switch to `logger` at that point, not before.

OPTION (a): create `packages/coding-agent/src/commands/extensions-triage.ts` as a thin `Command` subclass with a `json` boolean flag, importing the implementation with a TOP-LEVEL import (never `await import`), and `export default class`.
OPTION (a): add `extensionsTriageHelp` to command-help.ts using the `{ description } satisfies CommandMetadata` form.

OPTION (a): register the command in cli-commands.ts — one entry in the `commands` array. This single edit is what makes `runCli` route `omp extensions-triage` to the command instead of leaking the argv to the LLM as a prompt (the #1496 regression the module header warns about).

OPTION (b) ONLY, after step 1 chose (b): in capability/index.ts change `seen` to a `Map<string, T & { _source: SourceMeta }>`, change the two `deduped.some(...)` alias computations to `.find(...)`, and at each `_shadowed = true` site assign the winner — `seen.get(key)` for the keySeen branch, the `.find()` hit for the aliasSeen branch. Also `seen.set(key, item)` on the survivor path and the suppressed path. Update the repeated inline intersection types at :144/:145/:146/:211/:218 and the public one at types.ts:165 to carry `_shadowedBy`.

OPTION (b) ONLY: thread the winner into state-manager. Supply `getShadowedBy` at all SIX addItems call sites, and hand-wire the same read at the three hand-built row sites (mcp :180, hook :236, context-file :267) which bypass addItems entirely. Missing any one leaves that kind permanently undefined — and because the field is optional and silently absent, nothing will fail loudly.

Write the contract test. Fixture: one skill with the SAME name present at both user and project level, so exactly one row is shadowed; plus one row blocked by a provider disable so a `disabledReason` is populated. Assert the triage question, not the field names: (1) every discovered extension appears exactly once, keyed by id; (2) each row's state is one of the real `ExtensionState` values; (3) a shadowed row exists AND its `shadowedBy` is undefined — under (a) that is the documented contract a future refactor must be told to revisit, under (b) it is the regression proving the winner was recorded; (4) a policy-disabled row carries a non-empty `disabledReason` different from `"shadowed"`. Do NOT assert that `shadowedBy` is undefined as a permanent truth — assert the option-appropriate direction.

Run the gate: `bun run check:ts`, then `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/extensions-triage-cli.test.ts`. Do NOT use the plan's `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/ -t 'acp'` — see plan_corrections #4; that filter matches test NAMES, and a triage test is not named 'acp', so the command would pass without ever running the new code. If the native addon is unbuilt, `bun test` reports 0 pass with 'Failed to load pi_natives native addon for darwin-arm64'; build it or treat the test as not yet run.

Sanity-run the real binary against a real tree: `omp extensions-triage` and `omp extensions-triage --json`, and compare the row set against the `/extensions` dashboard for the same cwd. They must agree. Disagreement means the disabledIds mirroring in step 4 is wrong. Only after that passes, request the Wave D changelog authorization and add the one-line CHANGELOG entry.

test_contract: The observable contract is: given a fixture tree where one skill exists at two precedence levels and one extension is blocked by a disable policy, `omp extensions-triage` (and its `--json` form) emits exactly one row per discovered extension, each carrying a state drawn from the real state union and, for anything not active, the reason — and the row set matches what the `/extensions` dashboard shows for the same cwd. If this regresses, a user whose plugin silently failed to load is told the plugin loaded and is active, so they debug the wrong layer entirely: the whole purpose of the command is to make 'loaded but blocked, and blocked by what' answerable without opening the TUI. Under option (a) there is a second, deliberate contract: a shadowed row reports `shadowedBy === undefined`, which pins the current gap so a later refactor that starts populating it knows to revisit this test instead of silently changing what the CLI claims. Under option (b) that same assertion inverts into the regression test for the fix: a shadowed row MUST name its shadow source, and if a refactor reintroduces a bare `item._shadowed = true` the test goes red instead of the field quietly going back to undefined.
test_files: packages/coding-agent/test/extensions-discovery.test.ts (read for fixture helpers; do not duplicate)
packages/coding-agent/test/discovery/disabled-extensions.test.ts (read for the disable-policy fixture; do not duplicate)
OPTION (b): packages/coding-agent/test/capability/*.test.ts — the winner-recording assertion belongs in the capability suite, at the layer that owns `seen`/`deduped`, not through the CLI

MANUAL (not automatable in-process): run the built binary, `omp extensions-triage --json`, and diff its row set against the /extensions dashboard for the same cwd
gate: The item is DONE when all of: (1) `bun run check:ts` is clean; (2) `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/extensions-triage-cli.test.ts` passes; (3) the manual diff in step 13 shows the CLI's rows matching the dashboard exactly — specifically, a row the dashboard calls `disabled` is not reported `active` by the CLI, which is the only thing that catches the step-4 mirroring mistake; (4) for (b), a fixture row shadowed by a same-name winner reports a non-empty `shadowedBy` AND a test in the capability suite fails if `_shadowed` is set without the winner; (5) the CHANGELOG line exists and Wave D's `shippable: false` authorization has been granted in writing. Condition (3) is the one that cannot be faked: delete the `Settings.init()` / `cfgDisabledExtensions` mirroring from the CLI and the JSON output will still look plausible, but every item-level disable will flip to `active` and the diff against the dashboard will show it. What the gate does NOT catch, and a reviewer must confirm by eye: whether the new `Command` was actually registered in `cli-commands.ts` — a missing registry entry makes `omp extensions-triage` fall through to `runCli` and forward the argv to the LLM as a prompt (the #1496 regression), and no test listed here would notice. The plan's own suggested command, `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/ -t 'acp'`, would go green against every one of these defects; see plan_corrections #5.

plan_corrections.claim: The root cause is `packages/coding-agent/src/capability/index.ts:247` and `:271`, where `item._shadowed = true` is assigned as a bare boolean and the winner is discarded.
plan_corrections.verdict: CONFIRMED, with a material addition the plan omits.
plan_corrections.correction: The two `_shadowed = true` sites are exactly at :247 and :271 as claimed — but recovering the winner requires THREE more edits the plan does not mention, or the fix compiles and silently does nothing. (i) `seen` is declared `const seen = new Set<string>()` at :228 — keys only, no item reference, so the `keySeen` branch at :242/:264 has nothing to name. It must become a `Map<string, T & { _source: SourceMeta }>`, with `seen.add(key)` at :255 and :265 becoming `seen.set(key, item)`. (ii) `aliasSeen` is computed with `deduped.some(...)` at :246 and :269, which returns a boolean, not the matching element — both must become `.find(...)`. (iii) the inline intersection types at index.ts:144, :145, :146, :211, :218 and the public one at types.ts:165 all declare `_shadowed?: boolean` and must gain the new field, or the assignment does not type-check. An engineer following the plan literally produces code that passes `bun run check:ts` and reports `undefined` forever.
plan_corrections.evidence: `grep -n 'seen = new Set<string>\|deduped.some\|seen.has(key)\|seen.add(key)\|_shadowed = true' packages/coding-agent/src/capability/index.ts` → 228, 242, 243, 246, 247, 255, 264, 265, 266, 269, 271, 273. `sed -n '274,320p'` confirms the survivor path at :273. `sed -n '150,180p' packages/coding-agent/src/capability/types.ts` confirms `all: Array<T & { _source: SourceMeta; _shadowed?: boolean }>` at :165. Also confirmed by the same grep: `return { items: deduped, all: ...allItems }` at :290-295 — shadowed items are excluded from `items` but ARE present in `all`, which is what `loadAllExtensions` reads. So shadowed rows really do reach the CLI with `state: "shadowed"`.

plan_corrections.verdict: MISLEADING — the name is overloaded across three unrelated subsystems.
plan_corrections.correction: Before touching this, know that `shadowedBy` already means two other things in this codebase and neither is the capability-shadowing the plan is about: marketplace plugin summaries use `shadowedBy?: "project"` (packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/plugins/marketplace/types.ts:196, documented at :188) rendered by builtin-marketplace.ts and plugin-settings.ts; and the internal user-config protocol uses `shadowedBy?: string` to mean 'your user config is overridden by your project config' (packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/cfg-protocol.ts:83, rendered at interactive-mode.ts:5970-5971). Only the tui extensions `Extension.shadowedBy` is the one this item is about. Conflating them is the easiest mistake in this file and would produce an inventory that reports plugin-scope shadowing as if it were capability shadowing.
plan_corrections.evidence: `git grep -rn 'shadowedBy' -- packages/` returns 35 hits across six distinct subsystems; the three cited above are at marketplace/types.ts:196, cfg-protocol.ts:83, and tui/overlays/extensions/types.ts:68 respectively.
